questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was a very different location to what i am used to.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The most crucial information was sent to us via email, such as applying for courses etc. The buddy system was also very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: roundtour and information, mainly about the buddy-group social activities, by the buddy system members.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I just google student housing and found the cheapest nearby. I would recommend trying to not go for the absolute cheapest option, since that is what i did. I ended up basically not saving any money because almost the entire deposit was taken.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Sillim is a good area to look for affordable housing and it is close to campus with good public transport location. Ideally, you should find a place that is close to a station on the green metroline best case Seoul national University station

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You will have to sign up for a specific building/ major that you belong to. Notice that there are two seperate campuses only one is actually in Seoul. It basically does not matter at all what major you choose as you are not really guaranteed being offered courses in english related to your major.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can send emails with questions, but often the people answering them are not great at answering english questions

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not many english classes are available, so you have to be very flexible with the subjects you choose

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be flexible with your courses and dont put too much effort into choosing what building and major to apply to.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The workload on most courses that focus on presentations in english is not very high. Engineering and maths classes are very hard and time consuming.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In my opinion overall worse. The teachers are generally not very good at facilitating discussions, the lectures can be very focused on lectures where you learn very superficial facts about the subject. Also some teachers will switch to korean during the english lectures or take questions in korean without translating for prolonged periods.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Food Safety
Topics on soil science (Fate of organics)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Topics on soil science (Fate of organics). Very nice course on climate change the professor is very good at facilitating discussion and also good at keeping the lectures in english.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Expect that you have to buy everything for your apartment and expect that you will have to pay almost your entire deposit.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Almost every item is very cheap to buy except for food in grocery stores. It makes more sense to always buy ready made food or eating out. The main canteen has very cheap meals that you can purchase for lunch and even breakfast.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Except for the buddy system all clubs are generally in korean.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Korean language classes and the buddy programme

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the buddy-programme

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Busan and Jeju are both very nice destinations and it is very cheap to fly within korea. I found the DMZ tour to be very interesting as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty difficult because of the language barrier

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: not really

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language was a big challenge

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and drinking culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
apply for you foreigner registration as early as possible preferably book a time before you leave for Korea.
If you want to apply for the dorm you dont need to get an x-ray for TB you can get the blood test.
Dont expect to cook food
